name: Question 12
problem:
Let $X$ be the number obtained by a spinner with six sections labeled $1,2,3,4,5,6.$ The probability mass function $f(x)$ of $X$ is shown in the table below. What is $\text{Var}[X]?$

| $x$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ | $5$ | $6$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $\frac{1}{8}$ | $\frac{1}{4}$ | $\frac{3}{8}$ | $\frac{1}{16}$ | $\frac{1}{8}$ | $\frac{1}{16}$ |
worked_solution:
We can compute the variance of a discrete random variable $X$ using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

First, we compute $\text{E}[X].$ Summing up the products of each value of $X$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & =1\cdot f(1)+2\cdot f(2)+3\cdot f(3)+4\cdot f(4)+5\cdot f(5)+6\cdot f(6) \\  & =1(\frac{1}{8})+2(\frac{1}{4})+3(\frac{3}{8})+4(\frac{1}{16})+5(\frac{1}{8})+6(\frac{1}{16}) \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}].$ Summing up the products of each value of ${X}^{2}$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={1}^{2}\cdot f(1)+{2}^{2}\cdot f(2)+{3}^{2}\cdot f(3)+{4}^{2}\cdot f(4)+{5}^{2}\cdot f(5)+{6}^{2}\cdot f(6) \\  & =1(\frac{1}{8})+4(\frac{1}{4})+9(\frac{3}{8})+16(\frac{1}{16})+25(\frac{1}{8})+36(\frac{1}{16}) \\  & =\frac{87}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{87}{8}-{3}^{2} \\  & =\frac{87}{8}-9 \\  & =\frac{15}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 12
?

Let X be the number obtained by a spinner with six sections labeled 1,2,3,4,5,6. The probability mass function f(x) of X is shown in the table below. What is Var[X]?

x 1 2 3 4 5 6
f(x) 18 14 38 116 18 116
a
158
b
638
c
878
d
1118
e
3
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We can compute the variance of a discrete random variable X using the following formula:

Var[X]=E[X2]−E[X]2

First, we compute E[X]. Summing up the products of each value of X and its associated probability, we get

E[X]=1⋅f(1)+2⋅f(2)+3⋅f(3)+4⋅f(4)+5⋅f(5)+6⋅f(6)=1(18)+2(14)+3(38)+4(116)+5(18)+6(116)=3.

Next, we compute E[X2]. Summing up the products of each value of X2 and its associated probability, we get

E[X2]=12⋅f(1)+22⋅f(2)+32⋅f(3)+42⋅f(4)+52⋅f(5)+62⋅f(6)=1(18)+4(14)+9(38)+16(116)+25(18)+36(116)=878.

Therefore,

Var[X]=E[X2]−E[X]2=878−32=878−9=158.
